analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. Changes concern residency and availability (A-018, TB-007, TB-012, T-059), not visible prompt encryption, cache scope/crypto, billing, credentials or artifact qualification. No concrete regression is established in this scope.
ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift:213 now records selected victims after successful unload; existing ownership and cancellation checks surround it. ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift:22 adds recovery attempts to the busy fence used by command rejection and reporting. ProviderLoop+AutopilotControl.swift:80 refreshes saved enabled models without itself changing consent or control revision. New ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift:25-33 requires an unprotected, valid adoption, no live hold and serving-only exclusions; release is delayed 600 seconds and bounded by dwell and lease. Lines 41-48 withdraw adoption and rebuild capacity/heartbeat rather than cancelling requests. This is an intentional availability-policy change, not evidence of unauthorized inference or plaintext exposure.
Integration must examine noteSelectedModelUnloaded, selectedModelRecovery lifecycle, savedEnabledModels consumers, and recovery eviction/admission callers: ensure config removal cancels stale recovery, attempts clear on failure, holds/pins/add-on fences are revalidated after suspension, and withdrawal prevents both local and coordinator admission while in-flight work drains. These implementations are outside this supplied scope. ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift's added head line 82 awaits recovery before authorization supervision; determine whether it merely schedules bounded work or can delay expiry/revocation supervision (T-053/T-057). Delay is not established by the call alone. T-041's cache cryptographic controls are untouched here; model unload/reload does not itself prove a change to cache isolation or purge guarantees.
